speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They have done well and I commend them for it.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: But even Olympians can improve, as Joseph Schooling showed us last week.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Therefore, in confronting a horizon that is rapidly changing, digitising and globalising, our Public Service will do well to keep an eye on the horizon and to see how we can move with the times, so that it can remain the enviable service that so many hanker after.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: In the early days of nation building, each Ministry's mission was rather well-defined and each could go about its own job to achieve its mission: MND to build good flats, MINDEF to protect Singapore's sovereignty and so forth.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Now, fast forward to today's digital and globalised age.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Though the basic mission remains the same for each Ministry, there are many "horizontal factors" that impact how each functionally-organised vertical Ministry should fulfil its mission.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Such factors cut right across, sometimes, two, three or more Ministries.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It will affect how our flats are designed, how many recruits the SAF will be able to enlist, the dependency ratio impacting retirement age, geriatric care, even burial sites and so forth.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This is an area where collaboration can yield very good results.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Through our various Government e-portals, there are valuable data sets that can be mined and put to good use to improve the Public Service in the areas of public transport, healthcare, urban planning and so forth.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: In this fast-paced digital world, our citizens are also expecting more from the Government.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They expect a single point of contact and a very highly responsive service.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The coordination among Government Ministries and agencies to seize opportunities in this new world and to meet the challenges that confront us can produce much better outcomes than if each Ministry worked on its own.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: One hallmark of Singapore's good governance has been the ability and determination to take a concerted view on how to improve Singapore for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It has never been about the parochial interest of a single Ministry or Government agency.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This may seem obvious, but such concerted whole-of-Government approach is often not present in many countries.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: In several of these countries, the Minister guards his turf jealously, but not so in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Our founding leaders did so, and our current leaders must continue to do this, in order to secure Singapore's future for the next 50 or more years.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: To support our growth, the Public Service needs to work as "One" and also to plan for the long term, as Minister Heng Swee Keat spoke about, and even as it tends to Singapore's immediate needs.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Therefore, the one-dimensional approach of just having vertical silos in Ministries may not work so well.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: However, matrix structures which have been practised elsewhere, may also pose its own difficulties.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I think, fundamentally, it boils down to the ethos and the shared value of the Public Service, that each and every one, in whichever Ministry you may be, must think of the whole and put it before its own interest.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I think, with that, Singapore will do well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Change has to be the only constant in our lives and it is also how we transform ourselves and our mindsets to keep abreast.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The Singapore Public Service is highly qualified and capable, ranks well in terms of effectiveness and regulatory quality at the global level.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The staff form a part of the Public Service leadership, helping in the formulation of policies for Singapore and upholding Singaporean interests.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: As such, the need for robust, versatile, rapid thinking, informed and sensitive individuals is necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With globalisation and a more connected world, our Public Service must be prepared with resourcefulness, creativity and adaptability.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How do we ensure our Public Service staff can: (a) continuously learn and develop experiential capabilities?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: (b) execute a collaborative culture across organisations and Ministries to reduce wastage, enhance efficiency and productivity, especially in the areas of procurement, manpower and budgeting?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: (c) share best practices over various platforms as well as keep open communications channel?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Here is where teamwork to strengthen various domains must come hand-in-hand with breaking down the unnecessary silos; and (d) be more integrated in our heartlands and the issues the man-on-the-street faces.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This is also where some form of sharing of databases may be sensible, within limits of maintaining confidentiality.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: In the early days, the Public Service created many world-class infrastructure, such as the PSA port, Changi Airport, HDB housing, Garden City, Intelligent Island, Jurong Island and so on, all of which we are very proud of.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: In recent years, however, competition has caught up in fast and furious ways.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Some cities might have even surpassed us in hard infrastructure, technology applications and people- and business-friendly regulations.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Singaporeans who travel frequently often warn that we should not slacken in our efforts to improve.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: As our society matures, so has our Public Service.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Our public institutions appear to be much larger, having more specialisations and divisions of work, longer command chain and slower decision-making.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: It does not help if our newly-recruited officers serving the public do not walk the ground, or those serving businesses do not understand how SMEs work.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Would he consider setting up a "Cut Red Tape Task Force" to simplify regulatory burden on our businesses?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How can the Public Service culture be improved to empower officers, young and long-serving, to challenge the status quo, take initiative and drive change?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How often do officers keep track of competition to stay ahead?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How does the Public Service learn from the best practices in the private sector to keep itself lean and mean?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How could there be more strikers in the team, borrowing a soccer parlance?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: The late Dr Goh Keng Swee once said of the EDB: "It's better to hold back a stallion than to kick a mule".

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Would this quote still be apt to describe the frontier-charting spirit of our Public Service?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Recent events that threaten the functions, privacy and security of our public sector are a cause for concern.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If a syndicate or an organised group has managed to breach one of our most well-equipped systems, by MINDEF no less, it leaves little to wonder how well-guarded our public sector systems are and how well-equipped our public servants are in ensuring the functions, privacy and security of our public sector systems.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A study done by Accenture which surveyed 150 federal, state and local government executives in the US, found that almost 90% of respondents agreed with the statement that "cyberattacks are a bit of a black box; we don't quite know how or when they will affect our organisation".

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Another similar survey was done with 2,000 executives from large enterprises.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is interesting to note that 78% of commercial organisation respondents are confident that its cybersecurity strategy will demonstrate valuable results, while 53% of government agency respondents are confident this is so.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even though these findings are from the US, it is worth learning from their responses regarding new public sector capabilities.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Last year, at the Public Service Leadership Dinner, Deputy Prime Minister Teo, also mentioned about the need to prepare Singapore and Singaporeans towards a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He highlighted that digitisation will transform the way we work and deliver public services.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He also spoke about the cross-cutting issues facing the Public Service and how the Service could work together to address those issues to ensure coordination and coherence across the whole-of-Government.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One of the CFE's recommendations called for the Government to harness data as an asset and to build deep capabilities in data analytics.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Yesterday, I spoke on the need for a mindset change in the HR policies of the Public Service Division (PSD) in the employment of persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: One was a speech by Deputy Prime Minister Teo in 2012 at the COS in which he spoke in the context of the re-employment in the Public Service for retiring officers.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I want to know if employment is, indeed, inclusive.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I want to ask and I hope that the Deputy Prime Minister will give us the replies.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: At this time, I would like to acknowledge that it is not going to be easy but I also appeal to PSD on its second core value, which is − Please go the extra mile; please seek feedback and suggestions and also assistance from SG Enable and the other organisations and, in your hiring policies, please dare to change and to learn.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have seen how ugly people − all over the world, not just in Singapore − can get, when they forget the basic grace and decency that make us human.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have also seen the best among us, the brilliant, the faithful, the generous.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Public Service works with the many publics when they design and implement policies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Service works in a world where people with compassion and magnanimity live cheek by jowl with the perverse and the mendacious.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The best, and the worst among us, and all those in between; it is a daunting task.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Civil Service needs to work in a world where regressions show you significant factors, where evidence-based policy-making requires you to review data and test assumptions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Service also needs to work in a world where there is more demand than supply of resources.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Ministers move the Bills, we in this House debate, but the Service must take a considered view.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Previously, we had PS21, a change movement launched in 1995 to prepare and transform the public sector to be future-ready for challenges and innovate to seize opportunities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There are three areas which I think we ought to consider: how to work together, how to work better, and, finally, how to develop public officers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, we need the different parts of the Public Service to work cohesively together, with a more integrated approach, to deliver more coherent services to citizens; second, we need to harness new technologies to better serve the public; and third, having the right skills to deliver public service effectively.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Singapore has become a very complex place to govern.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Population and climate change are cross-cutting issues whose impacts are probably felt in the long run, and not now.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have the "whole-of-Government" as an organising concept which is fine and sounds very efficient, but really, can we and should we mobilise the whole-of-Government to address a single issue?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The truth is, we can but we cannot do so without recognising that there are tensions between different organisational forms.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There are domain experts, and there are issue experts.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We need the PUB to work on water, but we need them also to work with NParks, MND, HDB, BCA and a whole alphabet soup of agencies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The following questions come to mind: how is the whole-of-Government working together today to ensure that we are addressing them adequately and well?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: How are the different Government agencies convening to discuss trade-offs and make decisions that are in Singapore's and our citizens' best interests?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: To take a step back, it may not even be the Government holding the sole key to these decisions; these challenges will need to be tackled at a whole-of-Singapore level.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Government needs to be able to partner with, and harness the innovative spirit of Singaporeans, businesses and so on, so that we can move ahead together.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There is still more room for the Public Service to be bold and innovative.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We can, for example, reduce carbon emissions across all sectors in a most cost-effective way.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Technology has transformed the way citizens live, work and interact with one another.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Many services and businesses have shifted to the digital space, with more transactions now happening online via desktop or mobile, and younger citizens are more at ease and satisfied with usage of online Government services.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Recently, I read that, at JP Morgan, a software programme can review contracts that had previously required hundreds of thousands of hours of lawyers' time.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I can imagine the nervous lawyers rethinking their billable hours, but I think this is an incredible leap forward and will certainly raise the expectations of JP Morgan clients.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We can, and should, harness the power of technology for public ends.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: With the increased expectations come pressure on the whole-of-Government to meet higher expectations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The ability to understand and harness technology to serve citizens better is the crux of this transformation of the public sector, and I do not mean just digitising existing processes and services to go paperless.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Lastly, I want to end with the public official himself.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Technology will re-invent business models and affect existing jobs.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We also expect roles within the public sector to change and evolve.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This need for continuous learning is also what the SkillsFuture initiative encourages and supports.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, it is important for the public sector workforce to adapt a vigorous appetite for lifelong learning and pick up skills relevant for new roles.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am also interested to know, beyond just developing Public Service officers, how the Government intends to support its officers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Public Sector is Singapore's largest employer and sets the tone for people practices across industries.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I hope the Minister can address these concerns of mine.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Before I end, I also wish to ask of us, both inside and outside the House, that we should also acknowledge the good work and high standards that our Public Service is known for and delivers consistently.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is always easy to critique and pick on every mistake, every misstep.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Let us give credit where credit is due.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If that is so, what are the following measures?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Province of British Columbia has used its carbon tax revenue to reduce its income and corporate tax, and they now have the lowest personal income tax in Canada.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Would we also consider doing likewise, which was also advocated by Al Gore who said, "Tax what we burn, not what we earn".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Economists have argued this could improve overall efficiency of the economy.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Naomi Klein, in her book "This Changes Everything", writes about how we are stuck in a capitalistic mode of consumption.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is a systemic problem, and Singapore needs a cultural shift to change our behaviour and habits of consumption.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Ground-up initiatives can make this kind of cultural shift and there are many such successful initiatives around the world.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We have examples like Singapore Really Really Free Market (SRRFM) where goods and services are shared for free, part of a movement to counteract capitalism and reduce consumption.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Laozi said: "生而不忧，为而不恃", which means we must be mindful we are not master of nature and master of all resources.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, let us be gentler to Mother Nature.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: First, let me thank Members for their views and their strong support for the work of our public officers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Over the past week, Members debated how to position Singapore for the future and move ahead as one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As challenges become more cross-cutting, the Government needs to be even more closely coordinated in policy formulation and policy execution, and to harness and manage our key national resources more effectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This will help ensure that the Public Sector is ready to help implement the recommendations of the Committee on the Future Economy and to take Singapore forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I want to assure Members that our public officers do work tirelessly to serve Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: There are many examples of exemplary public officers who go the extra mile to help those with particular needs or are in distress, from HDB, LTA, WDA, SSOs ‒ the whole alphabet soup, as Mr Seah referred to.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Indeed, we recognise such officers each year to encourage everyone in the Public Service to follow their example.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: However, no system is perfect, and we are constantly striving to do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Each one of us who serves the public ‒ public officers, Members of this House – and members of the public, too, have a role to play.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: So, each year, we also recognise members of the public who have contributed to making our public services more responsive and empathetic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I take the points raised by Members of this House in the positive spirit for improvement but I hope that Members will rise from time to time, like Mr Seah today, Mr Ganesh or Ms Kuik, to also offer encouragement for the good work of the many public officers who have worked hard and gone the extra mile to serve their constituents and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: So, it is in this spirit that, today, I outline four priorities for the Public Service: integrating strategic planning and execution; driving innovation; building new capabilities; and developing our public officers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Cedric Foo, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about coordination among Government agencies and resource management in the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Two years ago, I announced the formation of the PMO-Strategy Group.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Last year, PMO-SG continued its work to strengthen whole-of-Government planning and execution, supporting the Prime Minister and the three Coordinating Ministers to tackle long-term, cross-cutting issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As part of the consolidation and strengthening of the core centre-of-Government functions, we merged the National Population and Talent Division and the National Climate Change Secretariat into the Strategy Group.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As Mr Seah Kian Peng pointed out, there are cross-cutting issues which have longer term impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It frames the work of many Ministries − covering areas, such as the economy, healthcare, workforce, infrastructure and defence planning, as Mr Seah correctly pointed out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Most importantly, we will also continue to strengthen the Singapore family with marriage and parenthood measures to support couples to own homes and have children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo will update Members on these plans later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Climate change is another cross-cutting issue with long-term implications that will be even more keenly felt by future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Coordinated actions by all countries are needed to help reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Singapore played a constructive and facilitative role in the Paris Agreement under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change which came into force on 4 November 2016.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun asked how we intend to achieve this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have identified four strategies in our Climate Action Plan published last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will improve our energy efficiency, reduce our emissions from power generation, develop and deploy low-carbon technologies, and encourage collective action among all stakeholders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This plan is an example of whole-of-Government inter-Ministry work which was coordinated by National Climate Change Secretariat, which is now in PMO-SG.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We evaluated every single option, what the cost is to the economy and to Singaporeans, and what effect it would have on mitigating carbon emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Then, we lined them all up and chose those which were most efficient, made most sense for us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This is one of the measures which will be efficient and encourage carbon mitigation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: A carbon tax will incentivise businesses and consumers to reduce emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It will complement the regulatory measures we have introduced and provide price certainty to industrial facilities for investments in clean energy and energy efficiency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In fact, the way that Mr Kok described carbon tax in British Columbia, it seemed to be the cure-all for all fiscal woes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: If that is indeed the case, I am sure the Minister for Finance will be delighted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are not earmarking it for specific purposes to retain credibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: But Government funds will support measures, such as enhancing energy efficiency incentives and training workers in energy management.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These will help our companies use less energy, save costs and reduce their emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: MEWR will have more to say about the carbon tax and carbon emissions later on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our companies, particularly those with an established track record in clean energy and energy efficiency, are in a good position to seize green growth opportunities in the region and beyond as countries, including Singapore, take steps to reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan highlighted that the Public Service needs to be innovative to position Singapore for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our leaders in the Public Service set the tone for public officers to work together and pursue innovative solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Public Service has embarked on a transformational journey over the past few years to become more innovative, work smarter through technology, deliver seamless services, connect with citizens, and build a future-ready workplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We can always do better, we can always be more efficient, we can always be more responsive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: To further these efforts, Prime Minister Lee has appointed Minister Ong Ye Kung to champion Public Service innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Ong will focus on a number of key cross-cutting areas that require close coordination among agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For a start, this will cover two key areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: First, the review of regulations to better support innovation and entrepreneurship.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Second, adopting procurement methods that support industry development, and helping our companies and people seize new economic opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These initiatives are in line with the recommendations of the Committee on the Future Economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Ong will also work with the Public Service on further areas to drive change and innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The CFE had highlighted the need to harness technology as a source of comparative advantage for our economy and to protect our national security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Digitisation is creating new industries and transforming existing ones, such as finance, healthcare and corporate services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Within the Public Service, we will continue to use technology to drive innovation, increase productivity, and transform and improve the way that we deliver services to the public.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Currently, the responsibility for driving technology adoption in the Public Service is rather dispersed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are studying how we can better integrate our strategy and processes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This push for a more integrated and technology-enabled Government is crucial in our efforts to build a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I assure Mr Lee that the Public Service will do its part to help Singapore stay competitive and respond quickly to the fast-changing global developments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Third, building new capabilities in the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the Government's plans to build new strategic capabilities in the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Two key capabilities that the Public Service needs to strengthen are digital capabilities and engineering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I spoke about the importance of Digital Government earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For example, many of you would be familiar with apps, such as OneService and MyResponder, developed by GovTech in partnership with agencies to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: OneService allows Government agencies to respond quickly to citizens' feedback.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: So, not one app for everything in Government, but at least one app for one service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Through MyResponder, close to 800 volunteers were able to provide timely CPR last year, and I understand that this has led directly to saving several lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Besides using available technologies, these professionals will work closely with our Universities and industry to experiment with and create new products and services, and enable further policy innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It is important that Government agencies trial new technologies and be early adopters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Yaacob Ibrahim will touch more on our efforts to support cybersecurity professionals in the appropriate COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa also asked about building engineering capabilities in the public sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: They have partnered many agencies and research institutions to develop innovative technologies and solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: JTC, as CentEx for infrastructure and facilities management, developed their own integrated smart estate and building operations system called J-Ops.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: J-Ops uses existing sensors in buildings to monitor and analyse essential services and systems not in one building but in several buildings from a central location.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This raises productivity as our facility managers can optimise ops room personnel and technicians over several buildings and facilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: But on top of that, this system also allows them to use data analytics and predictive maintenance to pre-empt issues and reduce energy consumption.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This system has the potential to transform how we manage our buildings and facilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These are important areas to optimise our land resources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These CentExs will develop and share deep technical expertise within the Public Service and optimise deployment and development of these specialities across the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: To strengthen the engineering leadership pipeline, we have also introduced the PSC (Engineering) Scholarship since last year to attract bright and passionate young people to pursue exciting and meaningful careers in engineering in the Public Service.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Government's focus to build engineering capabilities has led to strong interest in Public Service engineering careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We also look forward to partnering the private sector and companies in building these digital and engineering capabilities in the public sector to further support Singapore's transformation and the delivery of public services for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As Mr Seah Kian Peng has pointed out, the Public Service sets the tone for progressive people practices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We invest heavily in the training of our officers so that they have the skills to do their jobs well, not just today's jobs but tomorrow's jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This skills-based approach refreshes our officers' skills and will facilitate officers' deployment within and across agencies to optimise job needs and job matches.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have merged a number of career tracks for graduates and non-graduates since 2015 to provide greater opportunities for career progression and development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Once an officer is on the job, it is performance and readiness for bigger job responsibilities that matter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: All officers who perform well and show potential for leadership are given the opportunity to participate in development programmes and be considered for higher positions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Public Service will continue to be proactive in implementing family-friendly practices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Public Service will begin a pilot to enable officers who are starting or growing their families to spend more time with their infants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo will be providing more details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Government recognises the contributions and experience of our older workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The public and private sectors, our unions and workers have worked closely together to provide guidelines for re-employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: To support those who want to continue to work, the Public Service took the lead to introduce re-employment in accordance with these guidelines in July 2011.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These officers will continue to receive their last-drawn salary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This is similar to the practice of most private sector companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Public officers and pensioners on older medical schemes currently enjoy medical benefits when they are hospitalised in our restructured hospitals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As a continuation of this stay, we will also cover up to 28 days of in-hospital stay at community hospitals from 1 July 2017, providing better access for these officers to the services offered by community hospitals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This also supports MOH's policy to right-site medical care in the most appropriate setting, depending on the medical needs of the patient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: To better support HR policies for our public officers, a new integrated HR and payroll management system is scheduled to come online by 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This new system will replace and integrate different systems currently deployed in several Ministries and public agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The system will automate many manual HR processes and claims, and enhance productivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our officers can also benefit from integrated and structured career development and learning platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong asked about Public Service employment of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I have asked our public agencies and Ministries to look seriously into this matter to see how we can do more and do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In recent years, we have introduced a number of initiatives in collaboration, indeed, with SG Enable, the agency set up to help persons with disabilities gain employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For instance, the Public Service posts up suitable vacancies on SG Enable's job portal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are also appointing champions among senior management in all our agencies to drive the hiring and integration of persons with disabilities in the organisations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We also partner VWOs to create job opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: One of our agencies, Vital, worked with the Autism Resource Centre to hire persons with disabilities to support the digitisation of files.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As an inclusive employer, the Public Service will continue to find ways to expand opportunities for persons with disabilities to take on meaningful jobs in accordance with their abilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Public Service has played an important role in Singapore's nation-building.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Even as we transform, we remain guided by the core values of Integrity, Service and Excellence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Public Service will continue to partner Singaporeans and businesses to transform our economy and seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will continue to ensure good governance and effective execution to prepare Singapore and Singaporeans for the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can I have an update from the Minister on the progress of the Smart Nation initiative in helping businesses, especially local SMEs, to identify and adopt impactful technologies to boost capability, capacity and productivity?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would also like to suggest that we consider setting up Innovation Centres or Centres of Excellence for key sectors where transformation used in smart technologies can make an impact.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And this goes beyond the current capability of SME centres or industry associations because the largest impact will come from deep experts who can identify industry trends, IP and research that can drive innovation at all levels − the business, across value chains and the whole eco-system, including facilitating connections between public and private funding as well as technology partners.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given how Smart Nation is strategic to Singapore's future, I believe that one-stop access to our experts in business and technology will be crucial to the success of Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Budget has put a lot of emphasis on our need for skills in adopting new technologies, such as analytics, cybersecurity and Internet of Things (IoT).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, these are primarily today's needs and today's shortage of skillsets.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Digital revolution leads to disruptive changes in the industry and the economy and there are also other technologies that are developing rapidly that we will also need to study seriously.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Its distributed ledger architecture could potentially disrupt our financial sector, a key pillar of Singapore's economy; as well as artificial intelligence, which can deliver much higher efficiencies and provide intelligence to systems, such as autonomous vehicles and drones.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Smart Nation needs to go beyond the technologies of today and prepare the population for tomorrow's disruptions too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In a more recent report on the Future of Jobs released this January by the World Economic Forum, it was noted that in the next five years, advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning and natural user interfaces are making it possible to automate knowledge worker tasks that have long been regarded as impossible or impractical to perform.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If we do not manage disruption well, it is not just about losing jobs, but the compounded difficulty to match them to new jobs in the digital economy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given both the positive and negative aspects of these rapid developments in digital disruption, it is important that we have strategies to fully seize the opportunities presented by technological trends and mitigate undesirable outcomes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must also consider how do we ensure inclusivity so that our seniors and those with special needs can leverage on these technology enablers to improve the quality of living and their employability in the workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Underlying this will be the need for the capacity to learn, relearn, imagine, create and innovate.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To succeed in the future economy is not just about providing state-of-the-art infrastructure or the latest technologies.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The difference will be the spirit of creativity and the desire to succeed.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will manifest in how all these come together to produce new products, services or new and improved ways of doing things.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This innovative capacity is crucial to succeed in building a Smart Nation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Take a country like Israel which is seen as being in the forefront of technology and innovation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Israel's culture, environment and keen strategy are seen as the ingredients for its success as an innovation hub.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As Singapore strives to build a Smart Nation, ultimately, success will be determined by how our businesses and individuals embrace the opportunities, address the challenges and innovate.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While the Government cannot do it all, the Government can play a significant role in providing the platforms to bring together a vibrant ecosystem where the confluence of talent, technology and diverse ideas happen and, most importantly, value is created and innovation becomes real.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Since then, we have been investing in infrastructure and implemented policies to build a supportive ecosystem and develop capabilities to ride upon the digital revolution.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: However, there are two specific areas where I feel we can do more to enhance the experience of our people.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Thirty years ago, we started cashless transactions with NETS.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Today, it can get quite complex and troublesome: take a bus or train, use the EZ-Link card; go through the ERP, insert the Cashcard; pay for lunch, wave your credit card.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: And sometimes, we get stuck in the carpark because the car in front cannot clear the gantry due to incompatible card.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Of course, consumers have more options for payment methods.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Would it be possible for us to streamline these?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Government take the lead to do so?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: A quick look on the App Store shows mobile applications available for download by HDB, OneService, LTA, CPF, NEA, SG-Secure and not forgetting our Singapore Parliament app.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Is it practical and convenient for people to have to download so many apps to access different key functions offered by the Government?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Would it be more useful if we have one single main app that allows Singaporeans to retrieve key information from various Government agencies?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: We can log in to this app using our SingPass and -factor authentication (2FA) and there will be various tabs for different Ministries and agencies.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: For example, the CPF tab could feature the member's account information and transaction history.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The HDB tab, loan details and application status.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The MOH tab could possibly become a platform for Singaporeans to access their critical health records and medical history.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: And we could even monitor our health with this app.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Our recent SG Secure app's key functions can also be syncronised with this main app and key crucial notifications can be pushed out to all users in the event of an emergency or MFA travel alerts.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: But also important is the real productivity and convenience it brings to our lives.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: After all, one key goal of the Smart Nation is to enhance the lives of our citizens.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry share with us if this plan is already in the pipeline and what we can expect in the near future with regard to this system?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We are in many ways a perfect place to test-bed new ideas and pilot and refine new ways of doing things.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is exciting to see projects, such as the testing of autonomous vehicles in various parts of the country.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Such technologies could potentially revolutionise transport and urban planning globally.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am encouraged that the Government has created an Office to pursue our Smart Nation ambitions.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Other leading global cities, such as Copenhagen and Barcelona, are also competing to become THE digital city.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given that there are significant potential economic spinoffs from winning the race for talent and ideas, how do we differentiate Singapore from these other competitors?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Presidential Council of Advisers for Science and Technology has put together a report on technology and the future of cities, identifying areas where new technologies have improved the lives of city residents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These five domains include development of autonomous vehicles, urban smart and green solutions, electronic payments and smart solutions for active ageing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Further, the Smart Nation initiative allows the Government to perform the role of lead demand and involves citizens and businesses in co-creating solutions to enable better living and build stronger communities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Have there been instances of private-public partnership to effectively leverage on ICT networks and big data to co-create solutions?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Imagine our parents with weak knees having the confidence that they will not fall down.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Imagine our parents who are weak physically, having been at home alone and, if they suffer a cardiac arrest, there is early medical intervention.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: There is so much that we can do with technology, so much that we can do with enabling technology.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: The schemes are exciting − what they can do for our economy, what they can do for our people.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: But, ultimately, it goes down to what it does for an individual.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: That is what makes us excited about this Smart Nation, not just how good it is going to position us vis-Ã-vis other countries, but what it is going to do for each of us in our individual life.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: How are we building it into our homes?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: How do we reach out to more persons?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: How do we reach out to increase the adoption of assistive technology in the whole living environment that we are in and, thereby, increase the independence of persons with disabilities?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are living amidst an accelerating digital revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a revolution of a much greater intensity and scale than the previous revolution that we have lived through, and there will be profound changes: changes to the way we do business, the way we live, the way we interact, the way we mobilise, the way we socialise, politics and the way we interact with each other as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Because the people and the companies and, if I may add, the nations that master the technology first, the new digital oligarchs, these people and these companies will have enormous reach because their market is the entire world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our political challenge is to democratise these new technologies so that it empowers all citizens to harvest opportunities in this brave new world and thereby spread the fruits of this harvest more broadly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you think about it, this disruption is already happening all around us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are already artificial intelligence boards which trade funds on the soft market.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These AI engines can look through far more data than a human being can, make hopefully more unbiased assessments, improve their learning algorithms over time and conduct trades in milliseconds.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In Singapore, protectionism and building walls are not a recipe for protecting jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, our only option is to ensure that our people and our businesses have the skills needed for the digital economy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: You have heard Deputy Prime Minister Teo just now explained to you.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Even within Government, we have an urgent need for new specialists in areas such as cybersecurity, data analysis, software development, user interface/user experience designers and network engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you take the private sector − take Garena, which is probably one of the largest unicorns in Southeast Asia, founded and headquartered in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They run a business in digital content, e-payments and e-commerce.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They are expanding rapidly throughout the region and they urgently need more people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we do not just need techies and coders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need people who can apply tech to the real world to make a real difference in addressing the needs of real people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also agree that we need to help our businesses, our enterprises, especially our SMEs, to identify and to adopt the new technologies in order to make them more competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is something which we will have to work through the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), because each industry will have its own specific needs and it is not a tech issue, it is an application of tech challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Minister Yaacob will share our progress in this and how we intend to build up the talent pipeline, so that our SMEs and our large local enterprises will have the talent that they so need.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The second thing is that we need to build more integrated digital platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: You will notice that I use the word "integrated".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have heard the calls for integrated Government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These platforms must provide us with the capabilities that enable innovations that benefit citizens in a real way and reduce business cost.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Digital identity or the authentication of digital identity is actually a very difficult challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And yet, if you think about it, it is absolutely essential if we are going to have secure transactions in the digital world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am glad to report that one of our home-grown companies, V-Key, has quietly been providing this technology, a very novel and interesting technology, to a wide range of companies, ranging from DBS to Alibaba.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you think about what we currently use today, we have got SingPass.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To be honest with you, it is not good enough.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And yet today, we use SingPass to file our income tax.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, so many of our Government interactions depend on SingPass.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to make sure that it is good enough as a secure digital identification system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have asked the team to look at three features in the short term.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One, to include biometric elements; two, to enable encryption; and three, to have open APIs so that SingPass is not something only used for Government, but that the infrastructure behind that is available to the private sector as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to do all these in order to engender greater confidence, to reduce transaction cost, to allow information to be exchanged securely and seamlessly to create new services and to improve customer experience.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Now, the point is we can provide these platforms, but we actually have to enable our companies to ride on these platforms to derive the competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Another area we are working on in the next year is on e-payments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We all have got too many cards and, sometimes, there is the incompatibility issue, it is really irritating and inconvenient.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Today, we have got contactless credit cards, mobile payments, smart phone payments, and I agree with the Members, there is a proliferation of mobile apps as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But yet, a very simple thing, like transferring funds from me to you securely and without cost, it is not so easy to do.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, you can look forward to being able to use your existing mobile or Internet banking service to send funds to friends.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The only thing you need to know is their phone numbers, and even if they have accounts in different banks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I know I am standing right in front of Mr Liang, and I know DBS already has Paylah!, but I want this to be open to everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui's concern about the proliferation of payment modes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree that there is scope for consolidation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I believe that we should consolidate at the infrastructure level, at the platform level, at the back office level, to enable compatibility.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do not need consolidation at the front office, the retail level, the front, the customer-facing side, because we want competition and we want choice for the customers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have actually been too slow in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Similarly, some of you may notice that if you go to retail points, there is a Unified Point of Sale terminal.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This terminal is a "bao kar liao" thing.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It can read all kinds of cards, all different technologies, including magnetic stripes, EMV chips and NFC chips.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are taking a similar approach for transport and we are piloting account-based ticketing.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Commuters can also use their contactless MasterCard and not just have to find the right EZ-Link cards for travel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If this is successful, we will bring this on board and bring in other payment providers as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Again, to make it easier, to make it more convenient.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For Government apps, I take the point that we want platform unification.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I am not sure we need everyone to use the "mother of all apps".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I have told the Government departments that if someone else from the private sector comes up with a better and more effective app that makes available Government services, we should encourage that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should not allow the Government to have the monopoly on app production to access Government services.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Another example is that we also need to get away from the agency-centric approach.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is an LTA app, NEA app and so on and so forth.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to look at it through a more citizen-centric model.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One way which MOF is looking at is to group them by milestones.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When you were born, what services do you need?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When you have a child, or when you go to hospital or when you work, they are moments in life; and you can cluster these services, make it more citizen-centric rather than agency-centric.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Another thing which we are working on − in fact, the Prime Minister has been pushing − is this concept of Open Data.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Government has lots and lots of data, including real-time data, down to the location of every bus and taxi.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We want to make this data available for free for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you are on Facebook, you go to Messenger, search for this chatbot called "BusUncle".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It was written by someone who did not like the interface for bus arrival times.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, this is a chatbot, you just send a message, it will tell you when the bus is coming and he does it in a very quirky Singaporean way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But actually, the real interesting thing about this chatbot is the fact that, beneath it, it is accessing real time LTA data for free.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is an example where providing Government data, having open data and allowing the private sector to ride on top of it, creates a whole new level of services that we could not have imagined or we could not have delivered with such style.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Most of this is by commuters who are checking bus arrival times on their apps.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: By freeing data, we believe, we enable businesses and citizens to innovate, to develop new products that will serve their own needs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We can still allow proliferation at the front end and at the top end, but let us create common platforms and open data underneath it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: From today, this is being launched by Grab, there is GrabShuttle.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am afraid it is another app, or maybe it is another side feature of the app.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What this does is that it allows commuters to crowd-start their new routes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: You can use this to enable private bus operators to use the same analytics to improve the fleet management and operations, including the tracking of punctuality of drivers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Public transport is hub to hub and then you have a last-mile issue.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you can make it smart, public transport can be revolutionised to be point to point, responsive and in real time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is how we can get a revolution to make public transport the preferred mode of transport and how we can get higher throughput without increasing our roads to more than the 12% of land that they already take.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is an example where we need to push harder and faster.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: While we do all these − make data available, allow people to ride on it, allow new programmes, the e-payments digital identity − do not forget that cybersecurity is an absolute pre-requisite.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our critical control systems need to be protected, even if we make them smart.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members have just heard the recent breach in the MINDEF system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I hope this now emphasises the point that when we decided to have Internet Segregation of the Public Service, it was absolutely the right decision.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Otherwise, that breach could potentially have led to breaches of internal control and secure systems.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I can assure Members that our civil servants still continue to be able to serve the Net.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, in my Ministry, we have ensured that Wireless@SG is pervasive throughout the building.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Everyone can continue to surf on their tablets, phones or on separate computers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, civil servants are not cut off from the Internet.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to bear in mind the fact that we need a renewed sense of urgency to uncover new possibilities to work across bureaucratic boundaries and to be willing to disrupt ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: From time to time, you come up here and you give speeches about how there are missing gaps in covered walkways and so on and so forth, because different people own different pieces of land.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I believe that the old way of coordination in a top-down fashion, although it can be facilitated to some extent by email, is still not the optimal way to organise it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has transformed land use planning within the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also intend to make sure that we can serve the public better, faster and cheaper.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: One example of an e-service is that it allows businesses to check the allowable and approved uses for private shophouses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the past, you would have had to fill up a form, send it in, wait seven days for a response.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Today, with this portal, the answer is instantaneous and − my favourite word – free!

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Not many cities in the world can do this, because it involves intense integration at the backend.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the digital world, you think about it, the short-run marginal cost − different from the long-run marginal cost − of serving the next customer, trends towards zero.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whether you serve one or you serve a million, your marginal cost has not gone up but your unit cost goes down considerably.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need our public agencies to systematically eliminate application forms, streamline processes, streamline information flow.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is the way we can reduce fees for routine services by working smarter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also totally agree with Ms Chia Yong Yong, Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Dr Teo Ho Pin yesterday on the need for digital inclusion, especially for the elderly and the disabled.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are not far away from the day, Yong Yong, when you will walk in here with an exo-skeleton, perhaps.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If there is a place we can start, it should be Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will allow family or caregivers to be able to monitor the activity, security and health of the seniors and to have peace of mind.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also promoting the use of assistive technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have set up Tech Able in the Enabling Village which I think you might be familiar with.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a one-stop resource centre on assistive technologies and devices for people with disabilities, for caregivers, therapists and social service professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MOE also provides dedicated funding for special education schools to procure computer facilities courseware and other assistive technology.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
